sugar.title: Hidden Sugar Detected
sugar.short_message: This product contains ingredients that act like sugar or rapid carbohydrates, even if labeled differently.
sugar.what_detected: BOTIA found: maltodextrin, glucose syrup, corn syrup, fruit juice concentrate, hydrolyzed starch, or dextrin. These are technically not 'sugar' but break down as sugars or fast carbs in your body.
sugar.why_it_matters: Products labeled 'natural,' 'fit,' or 'healthy' often use these ingredients to add sweetness and texture while avoiding the word 'sugar.' If you're watching sugar intake, these still count. If you give this product to children, these hidden forms are worth knowing about.
sugar.what_it_cannot_conclude: BOTIA cannot tell you how much sugar/carbs are inside, whether the product is suitable for your diet, or if it will spike your blood sugar. It only signals the presence of sugar-like ingredients.
sugar.source_note: Detection based on ingredient list analysis. If concerned about sugar intake, check the nutrition table for 'carbohydrates' and 'sugars.'

sweetener.title: Sweetener Detected
sweetener.short_message: This product contains sweetening ingredients that are not sugar. Some may cause digestive effects if consumed in large amounts.
sweetener.what_detected: BOTIA found: maltitol, sorbitol, xylitol, erythritol, isomalt, lactitol (sugar alcohols), or aspartame, sucralose, saccharin, acesulfame K (artificial sweeteners), or E codes E420, E421, E953, E965, E966, E967, E968, E950, E951, E954, E955.
sweetener.why_it_matters: These ingredients provide sweetness without being sugar. Some people use them to reduce sugar intake. However, sugar alcohols (sorbitol, xylitol) can cause digestive discomfort—bloating, gas, or laxative effects—if consumed in excess. This is especially relevant if you eat multiple products with these ingredients daily.
sweetener.what_it_cannot_conclude: BOTIA cannot diagnose digestive sensitivity or tell you if this product is suitable for you. It only flags the presence of these sweeteners so you can make an informed choice.
sweetener.source_note: Sugar alcohol effects documented in public health and nutrition literature. Individual tolerance varies.

texture.title: Texture & Stability Ingredients
texture.short_message: This product contains additives for texture, thickness, or stability. Often a sign of higher processing.
texture.what_detected: BOTIA found: modified starch, starch, carrageenan (E407), guar gum, xanthan gum, gums, thickeners, stabilizers, or fillers. These are used to give body, thicken, stabilize water content, or improve mouthfeel.
texture.why_it_matters: These ingredients signal that the product is formulated rather than simple. A fruit yogurt with xanthan gum and modified starch is more processed than plain yogurt. A 'fresh' sauce with carrageenan is stabilized to extend shelf life. Not inherently bad, but worth noticing if you prefer less-processed foods.
texture.what_it_cannot_conclude: BOTIA cannot tell you if these additives are harmful, if the product is unhealthy, or if it's right for your diet. Only that the product is more formulaic than basic versions.
texture.source_note: Texture additives are regulated food ingredients. Presence is factual; interpretation is yours.

animal.title: Animal-Origin Ingredients
animal.short_message: This product contains an ingredient of animal origin, or possible animal origin. This might matter to you.
animal.what_detected: BOTIA found: gelatin, pork gelatin, bovine gelatin, carmine (cochineal extract), carminic acid, E120, mono- and diglycerides (E471) when origin is unspecified, or other animal-derived additives.
animal.why_it_matters: Some people avoid animal-derived ingredients for ethical, cultural, religious, or dietary reasons. These ingredients are often hidden—a fruit juice concentrate may contain gelatin; a red sauce may use carmine instead of beet juice. BOTIA flags them so you can decide if they matter to you.
animal.what_it_cannot_conclude: BOTIA cannot tell you if the product is vegan, vegetarian, halal, or kosher. That's your decision. BOTIA only signals: this ingredient likely comes from an animal or could.
animal.source_note: Animal-origin ingredients are declared on labels; BOTIA reads and highlights them.

flavor.title: Flavor Intensifier Detected
flavor.short_message: This product contains ingredients designed to intensify taste. This is a significant sign of ultra-processing.
flavor.what_detected: BOTIA found: monosodium glutamate (MSG), glutamate, E621, yeast extract, flavor enhancer, hydrolyzed protein, or autolyzed yeast. These are used to make food taste more intense and appealing.
flavor.why_it_matters: Flavor intensifiers are a hallmark of ultra-processed food. They're added because the base ingredients lack natural taste, so they're chemically boosted to be more palatable. This matters if you're trying to eat less ultra-processed food. Research on frequent consumption of highly palatable foods—engineered to be irresistible—shows patterns linked to overconsumption. BOTIA flags this because it's a real signal of reformulation, not just flavor.
flavor.what_it_cannot_conclude: BOTIA cannot diagnose food sensitivity, addiction, or health impacts on you personally. It only signals: this product is formulated to taste more intense than its basic ingredients would naturally taste.
flavor.source_note: Flavor intensifiers documented in food science and public health studies on ultra-processing and food palatability.

enumbers.title: E-Code Additives
enumbers.short_message: This product contains E-coded additives. BOTIA flags them when they're relevant to understand the product.
enumbers.what_detected: BOTIA found relevant E codes: E120 (carmine), E407 (carrageenan), E471 (mono- and diglycerides), E621 (MSG), E950/E951/E954/E955 (sweeteners), E420/E421/E953/E965/E966/E967/E968 (sugar alcohols), or other E codes flagged for ingredient interest.
enumbers.why_it_matters: E codes are the EU/international system for naming food additives. They appear on labels in Europe and many other regions. Many people want to know when a product contains additives beyond basic ingredients. Some E codes link to specific concerns: E120 is insect-derived, E407 is texture-heavy, E621 is a flavor intensifier. BOTIA connects them to the relevant alert category when applicable. If no category applies, BOTIA flags it so you can research it yourself.
enumbers.what_it_cannot_conclude: BOTIA cannot tell you E codes are harmful or that this product is unsafe. E codes are regulated and approved. BOTIA only flags them so you can see what's actually in your food.
enumbers.source_note: E codes are assigned by the European Commission and recognized internationally. Check EFSA (European Food Safety Authority) if you want detailed info on any specific code.
